changes.now: Living under another name after faking his death, Frank Castle learns from a hacker named Micro that his family died because of a CIA operation he served in, and that his best friend Billy Russo knew. Frank tears the operation down, kills CIA agent Rawlins and scars Russo's face. He's cleared, and walks free.
changes.proposed: Living under another name while the world believes he's dead, Frank Castle learns from a hacker named Micro that his family died because of a CIA operation he served in, and that his best friend Billy Russo knew. Frank tears the operation down, kills CIA agent Rawlins and scars Russo's face. He's cleared, and walks free.
changes.evidence: In The Punisher S1, Frank is not shown faking his death: he gave up the Punisher identity after avenging his family and lives as Pete Castiglione while everyone, including Madani and Russo, believes he is dead. The one who fakes his death in S1 is Micro (David Lieberman), first after leaking secrets and again with DHS's help in episode 12.

owner_calls.question: The subjects stage 'The forgotten heroes in the Void' starts at Deadpool & Wolverine and, with no later stage, holds through Inhumans, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (Black Bolt), the Venom films, Morbius, Madame Web, Kraven, Spider-Noir, the Spider-Man cartoons, Runaways and Cloak & Dagger, whose subjects are not in the Void. It is true for Deadpool & Wolverine itself. Should it stay as a box-wide label, or get later stages (or a wider wording) so it is true until the end of the box?
options: Keep as is (a box-wide label for the pruned heroes)
Reword to cover every subject, e.g. 'Heroes from abandoned timelines, some fighting in the Void'
Add later subjects stages for Inhumans/Black Bolt, the Venom films and the other titles after Deadpool & Wolverine
owner_calls.evidence: In Deadpool & Wolverine the Void holds Blade, Elektra, Gambit, Laura and Johnny Storm; Matt Murdock, Frank Castle, Black Bolt, Eddie Brock, Morbius and the others in the later titles do not appear there.
